title: Cohomology properties of maps in (Cat) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's 1983 notes on the homotopy theory of Cat (fundamental localizers W, Serre/smooth/proper functors, open and closed immersions). This page compares two canonical ways of factoring a functor f: Y -> X and classifies each factor by the properties fibration, cofibration (opfibration), Serre, smooth, proper, discrete and mono. My reading of which functor carries which name is a reconstruction, not certain.

(1) Left column: the cograph (collage, 'cylinder') factorization. Let C_f = Y ⊔ X with Hom(y,x) = Hom_X(fy,x) and no arrows from X to Y.
- f^♮ : Y -> C_f is a sieve inclusion ('open immersion'). It is therefore a discrete fibration and a mono, matching 'fibration ∩ mono'.
- σ_f : X -> C_f is a cosieve inclusion ('closed immersion'), hence a discrete cofibration and a mono.
- λ_f : C_f -> X is the retraction (y ↦ fy, x ↦ x), so f = λ_f ∘ f^♮ and λ_f σ_f = id.
- The fibre of λ_f over x is f^{-1}(x) with x adjoined as a final object, so it is contractible ('trivial fibres with final object'). In general λ_f is neither a fibration nor a cofibration.
- The question '(λ_f, σ_f) adjoint?' has answer yes: Hom_X(λ_f c, x) = Hom_{C_f}(c, σ_f x), so λ_f ⊣ σ_f. Hence λ_f is a W-equivalence for every fundamental localizer, despite not being Serre.

(2) Right column, most plausibly the comma ('path space') factorization. Let Z = Y ×_X X^{Δ1}, with objects (y, x, a: x -> fy).
- f^♭ : Z -> X, (y,x,a) ↦ x, is a Grothendieck fibration. It is 'not yet Serre' because only the fibration property is known.
- φ_f : Z -> Y is a cofibration (cocartesian lift of u: y -> y' is (y', x, f(u)a)). Its fibres X/fy have a final object, so it is a cofibration with aspherical fibres: Serre, universally in W (the crossed-out 'ft' may mean 'fibres triviales').
- μ_f : Y -> Z, y ↦ (y, fy, id), is a section with f = f^♭ μ_f, and φ_f ⊣ μ_f.
- 'μ_f not fibration nor cofibration nor Serre?' is left open.

(3) The NB states:
- proper + discrete ⇒ (discrete) cofibration;
- smooth + discrete ⇒ fibration;
- but proper Serre does not imply cofibration, and smooth Serre does not imply fibration.

(4) The circled questions ask whether X (resp. Y) classifies the cofibres of f^♮ (resp. σ_f), i.e. a straightening question.

(5) The bottom diagram is a hierarchy of classes of functors:
- vertical axis: bifibration ⇒ Serre, ..., discrete, mono;
- horizontal axis: fibration ⇒ smooth on the left, cofibration ⇒ proper on the right.
- Discrete fibrations correspond to presheaves X^ (functors X° -> Sets); discrete cofibrations correspond to copresheaves X^∨ (functors X -> Sets).
- Mono discrete fibrations are sieves: Y = φ^{-1}(1) for φ: X° -> Δ1 = [∅,{∅}] (the subobject classifier of Sets), equivalently Y = ψ^{-1}(0) for ψ: X -> Δ1° ≅ Δ1. These are the open immersions.
- Cosieves are φ'^{-1}(1) for φ': X -> Δ1. These are the closed immersions.
- These serve the next page's results on amalgamated sums along open or closed immersions.
errors: The text 'X^o -> [∅,{∅}] ... Y = φ^{-1}({1}) = ψ^{-1}({0})' is correct only once one fixes that ψ is φ composed with the reversal Δ1° ≅ Δ1, which the page does indicate.

The attribution of names in the right column is uncertain. If φ_f instead denotes the section Y -> Z, then the claim 'cofibration ∩ Serre' would be false in general. The claims are consistent only with φ_f being the projection Z -> Y.
The question '(λ_f,σ_f) adjoint?' can be settled affirmatively: λ_f ⊣ σ_f. No error, just an open query resolved by a one-line check.

ideas.what: Collage/cograph factorization of a functor through a sieve inclusion followed by a retraction left adjoint to a cosieve inclusion
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (Thomason, Quillen-era homotopy theory of categories; Cisinski for localizers)
ideas.where_published: related cylinder constructions in Pursuing Stacks; Maltsiniotis Astérisque 301 exposition

ideas.what: Comma-category factorization Y -> Y×_X X^{Δ1} -> X into a section adjoint to a cofibration with contractible fibres, followed by a Grothendieck fibration
ideas.modern_name: fibrant replacement / path-object factorization in Cat (Quillen Theorem A/B setting)

ideas.what: Hierarchy bifibration ⇒ Serre; fibration ⇒ smooth, cofibration ⇒ proper; discrete smooth ⇒ fibration; discrete proper ⇒ cofibration; Serre does not imply fibration or cofibration
ideas.modern_name: smooth/proper functors relative to fundamental localizers
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Pursuing Stacks, Les Dérivateurs), developed by Cisinski (2004) and Maltsiniotis (2005)

ideas.what: Sieves as open immersions (preimage of 0 under X -> Δ1) and cosieves as closed immersions; discrete (co)fibrations correspond to (co)presheaves
ideas.modern_name: sieve/cosieve = open/closed immersion of categories; Grothendieck construction for discrete fibrations

missed.claim: The page leaves open whether the section μ_f in the comma factorization (and the collage retraction λ_f) are Serre. It also asks whether X, resp. Y, classifies the cofibres of f^♮, resp. σ_f: a straightening question for the collage. These are minor and answered by standard techniques.
missed.quote: μ_f ∈ | not a fibration nor cofibration nor Serre ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Marginal: such questions are settled in Cisinski's and Maltsiniotis's treatment of smooth/proper functors and in the theory of collages/cographs.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working classification of standard factorizations (collage and comma) of a functor in Grothendieck's localizer framework. The ideas match material later systematized by Maltsiniotis and Cisinski. Nothing appears new beyond a few minor open queries.
transcription_corrections: 'cofibration ∩ monomtr' is probably 'cofibration ∩ mono ∩ ...' (an abbreviation, possibly for trivial fibres); unclear.
The crossed-out '[-ft-]' after φ_f is possibly 'f.t.' (fibres triviales) or 'ff'.

In the bottom diagram, 'smooth cofibrations' is likely 'smooth ⟸ fibrations' (left arm), paired with 'proper ⟸ cofibrations' on the right arm. The right arm reads 'proper ⇒ co...' with crossed-out repetitions.
'Δ_1^1' in the closed-immersion line is likely just Δ_1 (the superscript is a correction mark).
